subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

A storm in a teacup
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. Unnecessary anger or worry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"A storm in a teacup"** means a lot of unnecessary anger or worry about something that is not important. (बेकार की चिंता या गुस्सा)

 
 
• **Example:** The whole argument was just a storm in a teacup; it didn't really matter in the end.
 
 
 
• **"Unnecessary anger or worry"** refers to being upset or anxious about something trivial or insignificant. (अनावश्यक गुस्सा या चिंता)
 
 
• **Example:** His reaction to the small delay was unnecessary anger or worry.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the meaning of the idiom "A storm in a teacup" is "Unnecessary anger or worry".

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **A hidden advantage** (छिपा हुआ लाभ): An unseen or unexpected benefit.

 
 
• **Example:** The new software has a hidden advantage that makes data processing faster.
 
 
 
• **An easy and pleasant job** (आसान और सुखद काम): A task that is both simple and enjoyable.
 
 
• **Example:** Being a tour guide in a beautiful city is an easy and pleasant job.
 
 
 
• **More than expected or required** (उम्मीद से अधिक या आवश्यक से अधिक): Exceeding expectations or requirements.
 
 
• **Example:** The students' performance in the exam was more than expected or required.
